newsitem.title: UK: BoE - Avg earnings growth may threaten RPIX target.
newsitem.headline: BoE - Avg earnings growth may threaten RPIX target.

text.p: Britain's low inflation environment will be threatened if average earnings growth continues at its current rate, the Bank of England said on Wednesday.
"Earnings growth rose by one percentage point over the past 12 months," Mervin King, the Bank's chief economist, said at a press conference highlighting its quarterly inflation report.
"If that were repeated over the next 12 months, which is quite likely, you get to levels that are inconsistent with meeting the inflation target," he said.
The government has a medium-term target of 2.5 percent for underlying inflation. RPIX, which excludes mortgage interest payments, stood at 3.1 percent in December.
The Bank of England's report forecast it close to 3.00 percent and rising in two years' time.
The Office for National Statistics said on Wednesday that UK annualised average earnings growth for November had been revised up to 4.25 percent from 4.00 percent.
Earnings growth stuck at 4.25 percent in December.
The ONS also said that a net 67,800 people were taken off the unemployment registers in January, well above forecasts for a 30,000 fall.
But King said the figures overstated the reality.
"The fall in claimant unemployment is exaggerating the demand for labour. Unemployment fell much less in the labour force survey."

The job-seekers allowance, a new scheme which replaced old-style unemployment benefits, is thought to have caused a backlog of claims, giving the impression that more people have found work than is actually the case.
"Nonetheless, the degree of tightening in the labour market has speeded up," King said.
